result:
I wrote `ClassUtilsAgentTest` at `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/ClassUtilsAgentTest.java` with 58 test methods covering every public (and the package-private `getPrimitiveClass`) method of `ClassUtils`, including boundary cases (zero/negative length hints, max array dimension of 255/256, max class name length 65535/65536, empty/null inputs, mismatched array lengths) and error cases (`NullPointerException`, `IllegalArgumentException`, `ClassNotFoundException`, `NoSuchMethodException`).

I traced through the implementation by hand against the documented behavior for every method (abbreviation algorithm, interface/superclass hierarchy ordering, primitive widening matrix for `isAssignable`, the `getClass` name-cleaning/array-dimension/length checks, `getShortClassName`/`getPackageName` string parsing, etc.), including one spot in `getPackageName` where the trailing `;` is not stripped from the object-type encoding (only the leading `L` is) — but this turns out to be unobservable since the subsequent `lastIndexOf('.')` is never affected by that trailing character, so it is not a real bug.

All 58 tests pass: I found no behavioral bugs in `ClassUtils` that my test suite could expose — the implementation matches its documented contract everywhere I checked.
